report.verdict: A marketing manager with strong lifecycle results, but a headline and About that undersell the work.
write_up: You’re a marketing manager running lifecycle email and SMS for a camping gear brand, with team and budget responsibilities too. The work is strong, but a common problem gets in its way: your headline and About lean on broad phrases instead of the details that distinguish you.

The welcome-series line is the model. You name what you rebuilt and how the first-purchase rate changed. Your earlier Fernhill job also names the move from Mailchimp to Klaviyo; that work can help tell the story higher up.

Start with the headline and About, using the lifecycle work already in your current job. Then give the Lumen Street job a little more substance. A recruiter hiring a marketing manager could understand both your specialty and the work behind it without guessing.

cards.line: Marketing Manager | Storyteller | Growth Mindset | Lifelong Learner
cards.cannot_tell: The title tells me your role, but the rest could belong to almost any marketer. You run lifecycle email and SMS for a direct-to-consumer camping gear brand. Put that work beside the title.
cards.example: Marketing Manager | Lifecycle Email and SMS | Direct-to-Consumer Camping Gear
cards.question: Which lifecycle campaign or result best represents your work at Fernhill?

cards.line: Results-driven marketing professional with 8+ years of experience driving growth across multiple channels. Passionate about building brands people love and leading high-performing teams.
cards.cannot_tell: “Results-driven” leaves your best result out. The welcome series and its first-purchase rate are already in your Fernhill description, ready to bring up here.
cards.example: I run lifecycle email and SMS for a direct-to-consumer camping gear brand with 410,000 subscribers. I rebuilt the welcome series from 3 emails to 7, raising the first-purchase rate from 4.2% to 6.8% over two quarters.
cards.question: What kind of marketing work are you looking to take on next?

cards.where: Fernhill Outdoor Co., Marketing Manager description
cards.line: Rebuilt the welcome series from 3 emails to 7, which raised first-purchase rate from 4.2% to 6.8% over two quarters.
cards.cannot_tell: This is the line to model the rest on. It names what you changed, the measure that moved and the period over which it moved.

cards.line: Supported client accounts and helped with reporting.
cards.cannot_tell: “Supported” and “helped” leave the account work hidden. Name the kinds of clients and reports, and what you contributed to them.
cards.example: Supported [number and types of client accounts] and helped with [reports and your contribution to them].
cards.question: What kinds of client accounts did you support, and what did you do for their reports?

cards.cannot_tell: Leadership matters to your manager role, but email and SMS describe the work you run. Put those specialties among the three skills shown first.
cards.question: Which marketing skills from your daily work best represent what you do?

fit.why: Your headline and current job name Marketing Manager, and your Fernhill descriptions center on email, SMS and campaigns.
fit.level: manager, the title and two marketing specialists you manage
fit.note: “Marketing Manager” is in your headline and current title. “Email Marketing” is among your top skills; “lifecycle email” and “SMS” are in your current job description. “Klaviyo” is in your Senior Marketing Specialist description. Recruiters may also search for segmentation and A/B testing; add those to your current job description if you do them. Marketing automation could go in your About if it describes your work. Move lifecycle email into your headline.
